Question: How should one deal with this at a restaurant, ordering a steak dinner with baked potato and actually being served instant potatoes instead, and the manager saying they had run out of baked potatoes?
Old_Answer: I spent the better part of my youth working in food service and making a living on tips and made a really good living too, I would be really upset at my manager if they substituted instant potatoes for a baked potato without telling me so I could then tell my customer. A good restaurant and a good server will inform the customer that they ran out of something so then the customer can decide what they would like as a substitution. While many restaurants do have a clause on the menu in fine print that states substitutions may be made or something to that effect, that clause really should only be used as a shield from abusive customers. It should never be a restaurants policy. As a food server I would not be happy and I would really expect the manager to comp the meal (give for free) or at the least give a free dessert or something to the customer if they served them a plate of food they changed without asking first. If they did not do that minor bit of an apology I would start looking for another place to work. Since restaurants do not pay much and I had to rely on tips I need to work in a place that lets me earn as much as I can, not tie my hands. How I would deal with it as a customer who was told by the manager they changed something without asking me first would be to politely say that I wished that they would have asked me first and then if I really did not want instant potatoes and ask for something else. If they did not accommodate me I’d still pay for the meal but I’d let them know that I most likely would not return. Honestly even if they just honored my request without apology I’d still probably not come back. Now if the manager apologized and offered me a token like a free dessert I would surely come back. If the food was good I’d tell others as well. Things go wrong and things do run out. Sometimes the kitchen makes a mistake so if my complaint is acknowledged I know it is a well run establishment.

This allows your printer to simulate gray shades by using varying amounts of black ink instead of color. Keep in mind that the quality of your print may vary based on your printer type; laser printers often handle this better than inkjet printers, which may produce grainier results. Ultimately, experimenting with different settings and shades in your document can yield the best outcome.
